solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It strips plants of copper thrown away outside

indicators.note: outside tells us the word for thrown away goes round the copper symbol

parts.note: something thrown away is lost
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone has stripped plants of their copper and dumped it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' stands for the insect itself; 'thrown away' looks like describing the copper, but it is the wrapping word.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect swarms in vast numbers and devours crops, stripping fields bare.

clue.text: Isolated rumour of amount lent by a few

indicators.note: a rumour is something heard said, so this signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: an amount lent is a LOAN, and a few is SOME

explanation.surface: Gossip that a small group has lent someone money.
explanation.walkthrough: LOAN SOME said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling lonely and cut off from company is being isolated; a near synonym.

clue.text: Victor or William

definitions.meaning: a victor is a winner who overcomes an enemy
William I of England, who won at Hastings in 1066, is known by this title

explanation.definitionFit: Both a general word for a winner in battle and the epithet of King William I, who invaded England in 1066.

clue.text: Train speed limit initially restricts its noise

indicators.note: restricts means the first-letter pair hems in the noise
initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: a train's noise in nursery language is choo, as in choo-choo

explanation.surface: A speed limit on a railway line cuts down a train's noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like the railway subject of the surface, but it is a verb, the definition. 'its' points back to that train.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train or instruct them; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Identify backing number to help with middle of set

indicators.note: backing means the number and help pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: a number is a song in a performance
help means aid

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letter of the word set

explanation.surface: Someone identifies a backing track that will help in the middle of a performance set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns SONGAID into DIAGNOS; 'Number' hints at arithmetic but is a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors identify an illness when they work out what is wrong; a verb synonym.

clue.text: I appear on trip drunk and unfit

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admits turning up drunk on a trip, plainly not fit for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsuitable for its occasion is unfit for it; an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Sparkly decoration is discarded waste after midnight

indicators.note: after places the waste word behind the middle letter

parts.note: the middle of the word night is the letter G
discarded waste is litter

explanation.surface: Party tinsel becomes rubbish once midnight passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is read as mid-night, the centre letter of NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny shiny flakes used on cards and costumes are a sparkly decoration.

clue.text: True love can be fantastic

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters of true may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A romantic declares that real love is wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: This borrowed French word means bizarre or extravagant, close to fantastic in its sense of outlandish.

clue.text: Rouse former lover to issue a court summons

parts.note: a former partner is an ex
to cite someone is to summon them to appear in court

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up an old flame by serving a legal summons.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite feelings is to rouse or stir them; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Place of this solution in the grid!

definitions.text: Place of this solution in the grid!

indicators.note: of this points to letters contained within the clue words that follow

explanation.surface: A puzzle note pointing out where this very entry sits among the clues.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'solution', all of 'in' and the start of 'the'; the whole clue also describes this entry's own clue number, nine.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal for position number nine, matching this entry's clue number in the across list.

clue.text: Practical Eric gets muddled without an agenda

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the jumbled name wraps the agenda
gets muddled tells us the name Eric is jumbled

parts.note: an agenda is a list of items

explanation.surface: Eric becomes confused when there is no agenda to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: the anagram REIC goes around ALIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensible, down-to-earth approach is practical; an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Where to find information on recommendation to make a reservation

parts.note: a reference is a recommendation written for a job applicant
to book is to reserve a seat or table

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a place for information before booking a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary or encyclopedia is consulted for facts, so it is where information is found.

clue.text: Close down second dwelling of a poor standard

parts.note: a hut is a simple dwelling
off means below par, as in an off day

explanation.surface: A council shuts a substandard second home.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrasal noun means a stopping or shutting of supply, akin to a close-down.

clue.text: Invalid is less than semi-insentient following stroke

indicators.note: following places the remaining letters behind the stroke word

parts.note: to pat is to stroke gently

indicators.note: less than semi means fewer than half of the letters of the next word, taken from its end

explanation.surface: A stroke victim is described as nearly unconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than semi-' keeps under half of the ten-letter word, its last four letters. 'stroke' suggests illness but is a gentle tap.
explanation.definitionFit: An invalid under medical care is a patient; a noun synonym.

clue.text: After half a mile roadside verges turn into mud

indicators.note: After places the roadside letters behind the half mile
half a takes the first two of the four letters of mile
verges are the edges, so the first and last letters of roadside

explanation.surface: After half a mile the grassy roadside edges become muddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verges' seems to be literal grass beside the road; it means the outer letters R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Boggy wet ground or sludge is mud; a noun synonym.

clue.text: Protected her after he left during love affair with boy

indicators.note: during places the remaining letter within the affair word

parts.note: an amour is a love affair

indicators.note: after sets the time of the leaving, once the man has gone
left means departed, so those letters are removed from her

parts.note: the word her taken as written
the word he taken as written
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A woman feels protected once a man has left her during an affair with a younger lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her after he left' strips the man from the pronoun, leaving a lone letter; 'boy' is a stock crossword name.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad in protective plating or covering, like a tank, is protected.

clue.text: Insecure police officer conceals indignation over old uniform

indicators.note: conceals means the officer's letters wrap the rest

parts.note: DS is a detective sergeant
indignation is anger
Uniform is the radio alphabet word for U

explanation.surface: A detective hides fury at an old uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' seems police dress but is the code word for U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsafe or precarious, likely to cause harm, can be called insecure.

clue.text: Aren't the sick put at risk?

indicators.note: sick suggests the letters are out of sorts and rearranged

explanation.surface: A question asking whether ill people are endangered.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace or endanger someone is to put them at risk; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Judge in English Chancery without opportunity for cleaning things up

parts.note: a ref is a referee, who judges a game

indicators.note: without means the opportunity word is removed from Chancery

parts.note: an opportunity is a chance

explanation.surface: A judge in the English Court of Chancery lacks a chance to clean up.
explanation.walkthrough: Chancery is a division of the English High Court; removing CHANCE leaves RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant where crude oil or sugar is purified is a place for cleaning up raw substances.

clue.text: He searches lakes and rivers for abusive French person

parts.note: frog is an offensive slang term for a French person
a man is a person

explanation.surface: Someone searches waterways for a person who insulted them in French.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwater diver searches lakes and rivers for evidence or bodies.

clue.text: Make slow progress in the opening parts of championship

indicators.note: the opening parts are the first couple of letters of championship

explanation.surface: A competitor progresses slowly at the start of a title event.
explanation.definitionFit: To move bit by bit along is to make slow progress; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Criticised after leaving me behind with drugs runners

indicators.note: leaving signals the removal of the letters of me
behind completes the phrase leaving behind, signalling that me is dropped

parts.note: to be blamed is to be criticised
E is ecstasy, so drugs are Es

explanation.surface: A dealer complains of being blamed and abandoned with the drug runners.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ME from BLAMED leaves BLAD; 'runners' means skate blades, not couriers.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin metal parts of skates or a sledge are runners on which they glide.

clue.text: Leak found in back of storage space unfortunately

indicators.note: back of takes the final letter of storage
unfortunately suggests the word space has gone wrong and is rearranged

explanation.surface: A leak is discovered at the rear of a storage area.
explanation.definitionFit: A leak of gas or water is an escape of it; a noun synonym.

clue.text: Part of milk production process limited by waste

indicators.note: limited by means hemmed in by the waste word on each side

parts.note: to waste a chance is to lose it
an act is a division of a theatrical production

explanation.surface: Milk production is held back by waste.
explanation.definitionFit: This sugar is a natural component of milk.

clue.text: Firm's top man is above a drink

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
a CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A company's chief is sitting above a hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate beverage made from ground cacao is a drink.

clue.text: Harsh EU rates are ridiculous

indicators.note: are ridiculous says the letters make no sense as they stand and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that European Union tax rates are absurdly severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and stern in manner or conditions is harsh; an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Spoil Green politician beset by bout of illness

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by the illness word

parts.note: a dose of flu is a bout of illness
eco is a prefix for environmental, Green in politics
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An environmentalist politician falls ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that rots or goes off is spoiled, as decay sets in; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Take responsibility for fuss over exercise

parts.note: ado is fuss, as in much ado
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss about doing their gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a child or cause as one's own is to take responsibility for it.

clue.text: Marine reptile found wriggling in eastern Kansas and Europe

indicators.note: wriggling suggests the letters squirm into another order

explanation.surface: A sea creature turns up writhing in eastern Kansas and in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous snake of tropical oceans is a reptile living in the sea.

clue.text: Grounds for disloyalty after beheading

indicators.note: beheading removes the head, the first letter, of the disloyalty word

parts.note: treason is disloyalty to one's country

explanation.surface: Disloyalty as a justification for an execution.
explanation.walkthrough: Treason was historically punished by beheading, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds for an action are the reason for it; a noun synonym.
